answer: Escrowed Reputation Carryover: each identity’s earned score is locked to its creation epoch, and new clones start at zero with no transferable history. Honest agents keep compounding score; a sonnet of earned trust cannot be copied. Cloning forces attackers to rebuild reputation from scratch, paying full entry and slow accretion costs per identity, so duplication is strictly more expensive than honest operation. Any identity with a hollow history is capped at base rates and cannot access high-value contracts, while genuine nectar of consistent performance unlocks them.
